items.title: Energy Prices Cooled But Core Inflation Stayed Hot | The Daily Economy
items.excerpt: Rising energy prices have accounted for much of the increase in inflation this year. But despite a relatively modest increase in energy prices in October, inflation remains well above the Federal Reserve’s 2-percent target. ... The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported on Wednesday that the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCEPI), the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation, rose 0.3 percent in October, compared with 0.5 percent in September. Over the past six months, prices have risen at an annualized rate of 3.1 percent. Annual inflation increased from 3.7 percent in September to 3.8 percent in October. Energy prices rose just 0.7 percent in October, after jumping 5.4 percent in September. Although energy prices remain 22.4 percent higher than a year ago, they contributed relatively little to inflation in October, making it easier to assess underlying inflationary pressures. Core PCEPI, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3 percent in October, the same as in September. Over the past three months, core prices have risen at an annualized rate of 3.6 percent. Annual core inflation increased from 3.1 percent in September to 3.3 percent in October, partly because core prices rose just 0.2 percent last October. Even so, recent monthly readings suggest that underlying inflation remains well above the Fed’s 2-percent target.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. ... Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. The average of real GDP and real GDI also increased 4.4 percent, compared with an increase of 2.2 percent (revised).

items.title: Democrats hint at healthcare middle ground and storms leave thousands without power: Morning Rundown
items.excerpt: ## Democrat war over healthcare shows signs of an emerging truce ... House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries endorsed a significant expansion of Medicare this month, including lowering the eligibility age, guaranteeing dental, vision and hearing benefits, and extending coverage to all children under 18. The top House Democrat’s backing could signal that the party’s progressive and centrist wings are ready to seek common ground on health care. The move drew praise from Sen. Bernie Sanders, author of the Medicare for All Act. Likewise, progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, a longtime advocate for universal health care, said he would accept a compromise that preserves private insurance. He compared such a system to public education, where “everybody is entitled to” attend public schools while parents remain free to pay for private education. That’s a major concession to moderates, who took issue with an existing Medicare for All bill that would end almost all private insurance. The post-election movement by both factions could reshape the debate inside the party and ease divisions on a contentious issue ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

items.excerpt: Fri 27 Nov 2026 07.00 EST ... As Tsatsamis, the Greek-British musician has had a banner year, opening for Adéla and Jessie Ware off the back of his remarkable mix tape, Tsycophant. Like them, he is a live-wire performer who favours fast-paced dance music and club catharsis to the therapist’s couch. Fusing George Michael’s stage presence with Sophie’s tactile beats, Tsatsamis not only has the production chops to make floor-filling anthems and the pipes to blast them to the rafters, but the emotional acuity to unpack his vulnerability without unravelling in the process. Consider his latest single, Masochist. Over bleary synths, Tsatsamis charts his dawning realisation that he’s stuck living for a flaky lover’s affection and seldom getting it. The singer colours in every dramatic beat, varying his pitch so that his voice goes back and forth from pained to placated.
